clue.text: Baked dish containing tail of black fish

indicators.note: the pie holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: a pie is a dish baked in pastry

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here taken from black

explanation.surface: A recipe for a baked fish dish with some black ingredient in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pike is a large predatory freshwater fish, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: To be good enough at sums, reps will need to be schooled

indicators.note: being schooled means being trained into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sales reps must be taught arithmetic to reach the required standard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is an idiom for meeting the required standard, coming from soldiers passing inspection.

clue.text: At present everybody is supporting king, wise guy

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting words sit below the letter for king

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
now means at present
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A clever monarch is backed by everyone at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who thinks they know everything, like a sarcastic wise guy.

clue.text: Diane's letter is contemptuous

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane, so Diane's gives Di's
a missive is a formal letter

explanation.surface: Someone finds the letter Diane sent scornful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dismissive of something means treating it with contempt, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Individuals entering country, Asian republic

indicators.note: the word for individuals goes inside the country

parts.note: India is a country
ones are single individuals

explanation.surface: People are crossing into a nation, an Asian republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like the definition; it is INDIA, which ONES enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a republic in south-east Asia, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Striker in suit married at church

definitions.meaning: something struck to make a flame
to suit is to go well with, as colours that go together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer in a suit gets married at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker in suit' paints a footballer at his wedding; the striker is the thing lit by striking.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is struck to light it, and to match is to suit or go with something.

clue.text: Gained an advantage over drunken sot on a demo in Spanish city

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next
a drunken word staggers out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the pieces go inside the city's name

parts.note: Leon is a city in northern Spain
taken as written
a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A drunk joins a protest march in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demo' suggests a protest; here it is a march. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal a march on someone is an idiom for getting ahead of them by acting first.

clue.text: I'm finished with old painting technique

parts.note: taken as written
past means over or finished

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are done with an old way of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying paint on thickly so brush marks show.

clue.text: Organ, new make

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An instruction to build a new organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to make money, as in making a living.

clue.text: Raced round leading, then gave up

indicators.note: the word for raced goes round the word for leading

parts.note: raced means sped
to be top is to be leading

explanation.surface: A runner raced round in the lead and then gave up the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop doing something is to give it up, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: Game in which castle, perhaps, is manoeuvred

indicators.note: manoeuvred means moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a chess game a castle may be manoeuvred into position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' looks like the chess piece; with 'perhaps' it is fodder. 'in which' and 'is' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pass the parcel is a children's party game in which a wrapped parcel is handed round.

clue.text: Bring information back about bow of ocean-going ship

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the single letter
the word for bring information is read backwards

parts.note: to report is to bring information

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a ship, so the first letter of ocean-going

explanation.surface: Someone sends news about the bow of a seagoing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REPORT into TROPER, and 'about' puts O from 'bow of ocean-going' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a troopship, a vessel that carries soldiers, so it is a kind of ship.

clue.text: InterCity rail fare, fare at little cost to the elderly?

definitions.meaning: food served on a train, read literally as food carried on wheels

definitions.text: fare at little cost to the elderly
definitions.meaning: a service delivering cheap hot food to old people at home

explanation.walkthrough: InterCity was British Rail's long-distance brand; 'fare' plays on ticket price and food.
explanation.definitionFit: The British welfare service brings cooked food to elderly people at home, and food served on a train literally travels on wheels.

clue.text: Complaint by social worker, religious type

parts.note: a protest is a complaint
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A grievance is raised by a social worker of a certain faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant is a member of a Western Christian church outside Roman Catholicism, so a religious type.

clue.text: Leave Adriatic port

definitions.meaning: slang for to leave or depart
A port city on Croatia's Adriatic coast

explanation.definitionFit: Split is slang for depart and is also the Croatian city on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Rant, cross about extra security for the house

parts.note: to storm is to rant and rage

indicators.note: the word for cross is turned round

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Someone ranting and angry about extra security at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A rood is a church cross, often the large crucifix over a chancel screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm door is an extra outer door fitted to protect a house from weather and intruders.

clue.text: Excessively keen reporting, though lacking chapter about English queen

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the letter for English
lacking means the letter for chapter is dropped

parts.note: news reporting is coverage
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Reporting that is too enthusiastic, though it skips a chapter about an English queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops C from COVERAGE, leaving OVERAGE; 'about' puts E inside it, then R follows. 'though' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be over-eager is to be too keen, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Release one rodent into river

indicators.note: the two pieces go into the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
taken as written
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone frees a single rat into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to release them from blame, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Shut up before greeting jealous husband

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
in a down answer the word is read upwards

parts.note: a door pushed to is shut
hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be quiet before saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TO into OT. A door 'to' is closed, a sense not all solvers know.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Othello murders his wife Desdemona out of jealousy, so he is the archetypal jealous husband.

clue.text: Take it on before performance

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: re means on or concerning
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a role before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take it' is how someone responds to news, as in 'How did she take it?'
explanation.definitionFit: How someone takes something is how they respond to it, so the verb phrase matches.

clue.text: Captain brought in an eastern perennial

indicators.note: the captain's name is put inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
Captain Nemo is the submarine commander in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A captain has introduced a plant from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant that returns each year, so it is an example of a perennial.

clue.text: In disorderly haste? Completely

definitions.meaning: rushing so wildly you tumble over, said of a headlong rush
utterly, as in being totally in love

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tumbling over in a rush and also means utterly, as in falling deeply in love.

clue.text: Where H may be readily available

definitions.text: Where H may be readily available

parts.words: Where H may be readily available
parts.note: H is the letter marked on the hot tap, and the phrase also means ready for use

explanation.walkthrough: On a basin the hot tap is marked H.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means available whenever needed, like beer drawn from a barrel.

clue.text: Girl in film is sexy

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A young woman in a film looks alluring.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a title and term for an unmarried girl or young woman.

clue.text: One about to be strangled by evil Italian criminal

indicators.note: being strangled means being held tight inside, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: ill means evil or harm
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
one is I, the Roman numeral
C stands for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be throttled by a wicked Italian gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, so it is an adjective synonym of criminal.

clue.text: Boat almost left with wrong load

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for left is dropped

parts.note: gone means left or departed

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A boat has nearly departed carrying the wrong cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GONE to GON; 'wrong' rearranges LOAD to DOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a flat-bottomed Venetian boat, so it is an example of a boat.

clue.text: Baby's left a wet blanket

parts.note: to baby someone is to spoil them, so the baby's of the clue reads as babies, that is spoils
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: An infant has been left behind on a damp blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby's' looks like a noun with a possessive; read it as the verb: babies, that is spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is a person who dampens others' fun, which is what a killjoy is.

clue.text: Wager involving singular footballer

indicators.note: the word for wager wraps round the letter

parts.note: a bet is a wager
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet on one particular footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: George Best was a celebrated Manchester United player, so the surname is an example of a footballer.
